wkd.period: Average weekday, October 2025 – September 2026 (SFMTA automatic passenger counts, 12-month mean)

outsideEntries.note: observed: weekday trips from each station to the 9 SF-area stations; model: all boardings there (the model only carries trips with an end in San Francisco)

caltrainRegional.source: Observed: 2024 Caltrain/MTC origin–destination survey (on-to-off study, weighted weekday matrix by station group) fitted to Caltrain FY2026 boardings by station, periods from the survey's counts by direction and time of day rescaled to the fall 2025 count (regional-od.json). An estimate, not a count: Caltrain has no station-to-station counts.

shareNoCityEnd.note: journeys with neither station in San Francisco (San Francisco, 22nd Street); survey2024 counts group 1 (4th & King) only, so 22nd Street riders are counted as having no city end there

shuttle.note: BATS counts shuttle and vanpool together, unlinked; the model counts shuttle trips only

ferry.source: SF Bay Ferry public ridership data, FY2026 average weekday; Golden Gate Ferry FY2025 (Larkspur: annual share × weekday average)

tripLength.source: NTD NTD report year 2024 (agency fiscal year July 2023 - June 2024). max(report_year) in the dataset on the access date = 2024; 2023 Muni values included for comparison.: passenger miles ÷ unlinked trips
tripLength.note: model distance is along the line between consecutive stops (straight hops), which slightly undercounts curves

timeOfDay.measure: Share of weekday BART exits (and entries) at the eight San Francisco stations by period
timeOfDay.source: BART hourly origin–destination, October 2025 weekdays (by tap-in hour, so exits run slightly early)

muniSpeed.note: observed: SFCTA CMP 2025, Muni buses on the CMP network (arterials); scheduled: all Muni bus routes, GTFS run times over their drawn paths, trip-weighted

modeShares.source: BATS 2023 (MTC), San Francisco residents: unlinked trip shares converted to linked trips; car trips split 55/45 driver/passenger (assumed)

avgTransitTripMin.source: NCHRP 716: mean transit trip time, all trips, urban areas over 1M with rail (2009 NHTS)

ivtCoefficient.source: FHWA 2010 p. 7-15 (FTA guidance); trip model (trips not from home, visitors) and, per leg of a home-based tour, TM1 tour model (summed over both legs)

nestCoefficients.source: FHWA 2010 §7 (one scale, 0.72 from TM1, for the auto and non-motorized nests)

tripsPerHousehold.note: model counts trips with an end in San Francisco, residents and visitors

sensitivity.source: TCRP 95 ch. 12 (bus fares ≈ −0.40; range −0.12 to −0.85); UK TAG M2.1 bus −0.35 to −0.9; central cities over 1M ≈ −0.24
TCRP 95 ch. 9: service frequency elasticity ≈ +0.5 (clusters near +0.3 and +1.0); headways under 10 min: headway elasticity ≈ −0.22
TCRP 95 ch. 9: service frequency elasticity ≈ +0.5 (clusters near +0.3 and +1.0); headways under 10 min: headway elasticity ≈ −0.22
TCRP 95 ch. 9: service frequency elasticity ≈ +0.5 (clusters near +0.3 and +1.0); headways under 10 min: headway elasticity ≈ −0.22
TCRP 95 ch. 9: service frequency elasticity ≈ +0.5 (clusters near +0.3 and +1.0); headways under 10 min: headway elasticity ≈ −0.22
UK TAG M2.1: car fuel cost elasticity of car-km −0.15 to −0.35
Indicative: TCRP 95 reports ridership gains from bus priority roughly proportional to travel-time savings (elasticity −0.3 to −0.9 range used here as a reasonableness band)

benchmarks.model: MTC Travel Model One (2005 base, 2011 report)

ctc.source: California Transportation Commission, RTP Guidelines 2017 p. 49 (2024 p. 55)

fhwaTransit.source: FHWA Travel Model Validation and Reasonableness Checking Manual, 2nd ed. (2010), Table 9.9 (Florida)

tag.source: UK DfT TAG M3.2 (2024): individual services within ±25% for 95%
